key_insight: ConSDL discovers more reproducible concepts by replacing a sparse autoencoder’s single-pass linear encoder with per-sample sparse coding.
engineering_relevance: More consistent dictionaries and coefficients across training seeds can make foundation-model interpretability analyses more reliable.
method: Optimize sparse coefficients separately for each sample instead of using a single linear encoder pass.
Learn dictionaries through Consistent Sparse Dictionary Learning (ConSDL).
Evaluate dictionary and coefficient recovery and cross-seed consistency.
evidence_signal: ConSDL achieves near-perfect recovery across 16 synthetic settings and, across four vision and language settings, improves dictionary and coefficient consistency by 17.6% and 35.9% over the average of six SAE baselines.
watch_item: Per-sample optimization may add computational cost; the abstract does not report runtime or scaling trade-offs.
paper_title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
